definition: The Agents API is OpenAI's toolkit — an application programming interface (API), a way for software to request services — for building always-on agents without building the machinery by hand. Instead of wiring up memory, tools, permissions, and crash recovery yourself, you get a managed runtime: OpenAI runs the harness (the software wrapped around the model), keeps the session alive across long tasks, compacts context as it grows, coordinates sub-agents that split up the work, and provides computer use, tool calling, and MCP (Model Context Protocol, the standard way tools plug into AI assistants). It entered public beta in September 2026; the DevDay keynote added computer use, multi-agent workflows, tool search, and context compaction.

edges.label: the managed harness
edges.note: The API is the managed Codex harness — OpenAI maintains it alongside each model launch.

edges.label: powers long runs
edges.note: The goal → plan → act loop can run for hours or days on OpenAI's infrastructure instead of yours.

edges.label: tool permissions apply
edges.note: The managed runtime still needs per-role rules about which tools the agent may call.

edges.label: sessions outgrow it
edges.note: Context compaction exists because long agent sessions eventually fill the finite context window.

example.body: A startup wants an AI support agent that handles a ticket from first message to resolution — searching the docs, checking the customer's order, issuing a refund when the policy says so. Building that once meant a small team wiring up session memory, recovery when a run crashed at 2am, and splitting work across sub-agents. With the Agents API, the startup defines the tools (docs search, order lookup, refund) and OpenAI keeps the run alive for hours, compacts the conversation when it gets long, and hands back a clean transcript.
example.title: The support agent that doesn't forget

footnotes.body: Per OpenAI's API changelog, the Agents API entered public beta on September 8, 2026 with session orchestration, context compaction, and durable sessions; the DevDay keynote (Sept 29) added hosted computer use, multi-agent support, tool search, and tool calling. Amazon announced Bedrock Managed Agents (limited preview), which runs the Agents API's core capabilities inside a customer's AWS environment. Available through the API and in Codex and ChatGPT Work on Pro 500 and Enterprise plans.
footnotes.label: Release history

footnotes.body: MCP events were also announced at DevDay: connected apps can trigger automations when something happens in them, rather than the agent only acting on direct requests — the start of agents that react to the world, not just to you.

name: Agents API
tagline: OpenAI's managed way to build always-on agents: harness, hosting, memory, and multi-agent plumbing in one API.
whyItMatters: This is what turns agents from impressive demos into real products. Before, every team reinvented the same plumbing — session memory, recovery, sub-agent coordination. A managed runtime lowers the barrier to building agents, but it also concentrates power: your agent's memory, tools, and work now live on someone else's cloud.
